newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond and interest rate futures settled into a more stable rhythm after four volatile sessions, taking some comfort from a stronger Bund market and an opinion poll showing the ruling centre-right coalition would win the May/June parliamentary election.

The June bond future opened up at 128.70 and then traded in a narrow range, finding support at 128.54/56, yesterday's high, but failing to breach key resistance at 128.80 as traders stepped into to take profits at the highs.
June PIBOR climbed as much as eight basis points but traders said the contract was systematically sold by non-residents whenever it reached 96.40.
"We're condemned to move with the polls and it's imperative to hedge yourself when you take positions in such a market," one trader said.

The franc also stabilised after sliding since political uncertainty was first priced in last Thursday, general mark weakness in Europe taking the French unit as high as 3.3716 per mark compared with 3.3743 late on Tuesday.

Valerie Plagnol, market economist at Credit Commercial de France, said the CSA opinion poll released late on Tuesday, "was pretty encouraging for the market, but it's the first one and there will be a lot of opinion polls ahead of election."

She said the polls would create a lot of volatility in the coming weeks although she cautioned that French opinion polls in the past have been unable to capture the real intentions of voters, and projections of how many seats each party would gain are subject to a large margin of error.

Eric Chaney, economist at Morgan Stanley in Paris, also warned against reading too much into the derivation of the number of seats won from the percentage of votes cast because of the two-round system.

"It is extremely difficult for pollsters to extrapolate electoral preferences to seats, because they have to guess how many consitutencies would have a second round and then re-weight their sample," Chaney said.
He said his rule of thumb was if the ruling coalition won at least 40 percent of the votes in the first round they would win the election.

With the franc stable and little chance of a rate cut given the risk of pre-electoral volatility, most economists expected the Bank of France to leave the intervention rate unchanged after its regular monetary policy council meeting on Thursday.
French 10-year bond yields remained under pressure compared to their German counterparts, underperforming by one basis point. The spread narrowed to minus five.

Two-year BTANs, one of the worst hit areas in the selloff extended Tuesday's outperformance. The yield spread over German two-year bonds narrowed to 18 basis points from 24 late on Tuesday, reversing the recent curve flattening at the short end.
